subject: Termination Safeguards, Runbook Validation & License-transfer Scenarios
messages:
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@clarityhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Clarity Health Legal <legal@clarityhealth.com>, Clarity Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify: on-prem deployment - termination, runbook access & evidence flow

David — thanks for the quick demo last week. Legal here has a few gating items before procurement can sign an Order Form for the private on-prem deployment. High level: we need clarity on what happens to the runtime, model artifacts, and operational runbooks on customer termination (or insolvency). Specifically: 

- Do you provide a license-transfer pathway, or is the remedy a sealed forensic snapshot plus operator-witness session?
- If you do a transfer, what IP/license carveouts remain with Redwood? Can you propose specific MSA language?
- Can you commit to an audit window and evidence package (logs, snapshots) for our regulators?

We attached a short scope request (clarity-scope-request.docx). Our compliance team is asking for either an escrow-like *witnessed* handover or a turnkey transfer option. Can you please propose the redline language you would accept so we can route to procurement?

Thanks,
Michael Turner
VP, Procurement — Clarity Health
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: on-prem deployment - termination, runbook access & evidence flow

Michael — appreciate the clear ask and the doc. We can support both patterns but they carry different operational and IP implications. Attached a first-pass addendum and a short operator-runbook summary for context (Redwood_proposed-addendum_v1.docx, operator-runbook-summary.pdf). High-level options we recommend to present to Legal/Procurement: 

1) Sealed Snapshot + Witness Access (lower IP exposure): Redwood deposits an encrypted snapshot with a mutually agreed custodian. On termination or breach, customer (or a court) may request a witness session with Redwood engineers to enable validation and limited access test runs. No transfer of runtime source or proprietary kernels.

2) Managed License Transfer (turnkey handoff): Redwood grants a time-limited, executable-only license to the customer for the deployed model/runtime artifacts and provides a handover package (runbook, configuration, test vectors). This requires stronger indemnities, a defined acceptance testing window, and escrow of cryptographic keys.

3) Hybrid: Witnessed sealed snapshot initially, with a conditional transfer path triggered only after specific acceptance criteria and additional consideration.

For procurement redlines, we propose adding explicit language in the MSA Addendum around: scope of artifacts, rotation/retention of keys, acceptance testing procedure (15-business-day window), and a limitation on redistribution. Can Naomi and Priyom weigh in on the exact redline? If acceptable, we can provide a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Next steps: Naomi — any immediate no-go items from Legal? Priyom — can Solutions provide an operator checklist we can inline as an exhibit?

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: on-prem deployment - termination, runbook access & evidence flow

Team — read through Michael's scope and David's options. I attached a tracked-redline with comments for sections I think are necessary (redlines_naomi_v1.docx). Key legal points I recommend we insist on: 

- Carveout for Redwood core IP: the addendum must expressly state that any license granted is limited to the executable runtime and configuration necessary to run the customer’s instance; embeddings, kernel optimizations, and source toolchains remain Redwood Confidential.
- Acceptance testing: define concrete test vectors and a 15-business-day remediation window. If acceptance fails, customer may request a sealed snapshot/witness instead of full transfer.
- Escrow/witness mechanics: prefer a sealed snapshot with an independent third-party custodian (we list two acceptable custodians). Witness sessions must be strictly time‑boxed and recorded; access granted only to the components required to reproduce the customer environment.
- Indemnity and liability: if we transfer executable artifacts, require mutual indemnity carveouts and a one-time conversion fee.

One operational question: does the runbook include any embedded scripts or debuggers that contain routeable provenance to other customers? Priyom — please confirm whether the runbook package contains any customer-specific credentials or only generic operational steps.

If we agree to present the hybrid path, I think Procurement will find it more palatable; it reduces IP leakage while giving Clarity a clear path to remediate if Redwood is unavailable.

—Naomi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@clarityhealth.com>, Clarity Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: on-prem deployment - termination, runbook access & evidence flow

Michael — attaching a consolidated addendum that reflects Naomi's redlines and our operational constraints (MSA-Addendum-Redline_20261122.pdf). Summary of what's changed vs the original proposal: 

- We propose the Hybrid path as the default: sealed snapshot with third-party custodian + conditional transfer trigger after acceptance testing and payment of the conversion fee.
- Exhibit A (Operator Handoff Checklist): a phased checklist that we will deliver as part of the addendum; initial deliverable is a runbook summary (operator-runbook-summary.pdf), full runbook is redacted for proprietary kernels and delivered in a sealed, witnessable format.
- Audit window: 30-day evidence delivery SLA for logs/forensics after formal request, with defined redaction rules for Redwood Confidential sections.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS is preferable; if not possible, keys held in a hardware module with dual-control to be rotated on termination.

Proposed next steps for Clarity: legal to confirm if the hybrid mechanics are acceptable; procurement to confirm convert fee approval and acceptance-test owners; schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call next week to walk through acceptance criteria.

Attachments: MSA-Addendum-Redline_20261122.pdf (full tracked changes), operator-runbook-summary.pdf

If this is acceptable we can generate a DocuSign packet and provide the sealed snapshot routing options for your team to review.

Best,
David
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@clarityhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Clarity Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: on-prem deployment - termination, runbook access & evidence flow

David/Naomi/Priyom — thanks for the thorough redline and options. Procurement likes the Hybrid approach as a starting point; Legal has two small asks before we proceed to DocuSign: 

1) Please show the exact text for the conversion fee and whether it is refundable if acceptance fails.
2) We need an interim NDA to allow limited access to the runbook summary and operational checklist for our compliance reviewers.

I attached a short tracker with our clarifications (Clarify_Request_ResponseTracker.xlsx). Can Redwood produce a short one‑page summary of the conversion fee mechanics and confirm the two custodians you mentioned? If you can send a DocuSign link with the NDA and the addendum in parallel, we can aim to get procurement signoff the following week.

Also: schedule a 30‑minute legal-to-legal call — Friday 11/26 at 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

Thanks,
Michael Turner
VP, Procurement — Clarity Health
